V23: Within the existing native-file comparison scope, a normal attachment Content-Type that declares parameters remains unavailable when no native payload association can be established. Another verified attachment does not establish agreement for that record. Report WARN rather than N/A or aggregate PASS; definite mismatches still fail. Do not infer a new native-copy requirement when there are no native files; Source/Alternative exclusions and schema checks remain separate.

EMBEDDED_SUBTYPE_MATCH_XMP.spec_excerpt: The reconstructed embedded media type, including stream parameters, must match equivalent uniquely associated document-level XMP. Preserve case/spacing in parameter values; compare MIME tokens and charset case-insensitively. V19 permits byte/media comparisons for multiple candidate attachment records only when their valid size, checksum presence/value and media expectations are equivalent. Every candidate receives the same comparisons; this does not assign an owner or prove unique occurrence identity. Differing expectations remain unavailable, and body ownership checks remain separate. V20: MIME recovery must not fabricate parameter equality. Invalid parameter syntax uses preserved text comparison; malformed source values remain permitted. Source attachment/body summaries retain original Content-Type text and quoted spaces. Legal folding and encoded parameter equivalence remain supported; absent or empty body types retain MIME defaults. V22: A valid attachment Content-Type or its declared parameters fails when every possible native candidate has an available contradicting reconstruction for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required; any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Parameters are compared independently of the bare media type. Ambiguous parameter comparisons without a proved mismatch remain WARN/unavailable rather than N/A; they cannot hide a separate verified mismatch. MIME recovery safeguards, legal encoded equivalents and exact malformed-text comparisons remain in force. No owner, unique occurrence or complete inventory is inferred.

ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH.spec_section: EA-PDF 9.8.4 Table 19, printed pp89-90; 7.5 printed p44
ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH.spec_excerpt: Required attachment-record fields and internal owner/stream consistency are distinct from source-dependent fidelity. Original source matching is not a universal mandatory PDF-only rule; isolated sources may be absent and permitted zero-length stored placeholders need not equal the original attachment length. Supplied SizeInBytes and optional CheckSum must agree with associated native stored bytes even without a BodyRendering set or retained source. Differing candidate expectations or stored observations remain unavailable evidence, not proof of consistency. Collection member EA-PDFs are checked recursively in their owning email scope, not against parent attachment records. AFRelationship Alternative identifies a converted representation rather than the native attachment payload (section 7.5). Filename association and available original-source filename comparison preserve exact text, including significant spaces. Stripping path components, control characters or whitespace cannot establish filename equality. MIME parameter values are retained before get_filename() trimming; legal stored aliases remain supported by independent payload evidence. Source-assisted payload association uses the same unique email XMP owner mapping as body routing; similar Message-ID text from another email cannot supply source payload evidence. GUID identity retains priority. Source comparisons treat Table 19 records as unordered: reserve compatible original occurrences across the entire owner-scoped set before diagnostic pairing. Optional checksums and permitted zero-byte placeholders must not consume occurrences needed by other valid records. Equivalent assignments prove field consistency only, not unique occurrence identity. V19 permits byte/media comparisons for multiple candidate attachment records only when their valid size, checksum presence/value and media expectations are equivalent. Every candidate receives the same comparisons; this does not assign an owner or prove unique occurrence identity. Differing expectations remain unavailable, and body ownership checks remain separate. V20: MIME recovery must not fabricate parameter equality. Invalid parameter syntax uses preserved text comparison; malformed source values remain permitted. Source attachment/body summaries retain original Content-Type text and quoted spaces. Legal folding and encoded parameter equivalence remain supported; absent or empty body types retain MIME defaults. V21: Ambiguous association remains unavailable, but a valid supplied SizeInBytes or CheckSum fails when every possible native candidate has a readable contradicting value for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required. Any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Size/checksum observations do not select an owner or occurrence; optional checksum absence, shared streams, zero-byte candidates and Source/Alternative exclusions remain supported. This proves only the reported field contradiction, not inventory completeness or full occurrence consistency. V22: A valid attachment Content-Type or its declared parameters fails when every possible native candidate has an available contradicting reconstruction for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required; any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Parameters are compared independently of the bare media type. Ambiguous parameter comparisons without a proved mismatch remain WARN/unavailable rather than N/A; they cannot hide a separate verified mismatch. MIME recovery safeguards, legal encoded equivalents and exact malformed-text comparisons remain in force. No owner, unique occurrence or complete inventory is inferred.

utf8_source_header_review.basis: RFC6532 permits direct UTF-8 header values and defines message/global; RFC6531 extends mailbox syntax. Restore valid original UTF-8 bytes from parser surrogate escapes before comparisons, without Unicode normalization or byte changes.
utf8_source_header_review.boundary: Malformed/legacy charset values are not guessed. This is not complete SMTPUTF8/IDNA, normalization or malformed-source diagnostic certification.
utf8_source_header_review.message_global: Recognize registered message/global sources independently of filename extension, including nested-email attachment predicates and original encoded payload extraction.

undecodable_source_header_review.basis: A source comparison needs usable original text. Undecodable mailbox/text octets produce unavailable comparison and VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE, with independent supplied-schema, field-presence and readable-field failures retained.
undecodable_source_header_review.diagnostics: Escape surrogates only in report copies; retained source bytes and internal comparison evidence are unchanged.
undecodable_source_header_review.boundary: No legacy charset guessing, Unicode normalization, general malformed encoded-word recovery or complete source-parser certification.

uninspectable_source_review.basis: Attached originals with no supported matched email summary leave source-header comparisons unavailable and validation incomplete. Extra unrendered originals do not invalidate an independently matched supported email.
uninspectable_source_review.boundary: No new MSG/PST parser or external input inventory is inferred. Isolated omission and container-child checking retain their scopes.

ambiguous_source_header_review.basis: A source owner is not established by fields under test when that tentative source contradicts the record. Check every retained possible original for universal field contradictions or a Core Field tuple that no source can satisfy.
ambiguous_source_header_review.availability: Unknown formats or recovered source header inventories block the universal proof. Per-field unavailable comparisons cannot contribute a definite contradiction. Compatible or unknown candidates retain unassigned ownership and incompleteness. Previously consumed occurrences are not excluded from this proof.
ambiguous_source_header_review.boundary: Bounded by the configured item limit; only established header/size predicates are used. No complete source grammar, charset policy, independent provenance, occurrence assignment or attachment ownership is inferred.

nonsmtp_availability_review.basis: The V61 FOAF decision permits exact raw preservation or an unavailable-normalization outcome for non-SMTP original tokens. Such tokens cannot establish a missing SMTP Agent or a normalized-mailbox count contradiction.
nonsmtp_availability_review.independent_checks: Known SMTP presence, understood known-only mailbox comparisons, supplied FOAF syntax and supplied raw fidelity retain their own predicates. Additional SMTP entries that could derive from non-SMTP tokens require independent normalization evidence.
nonsmtp_availability_review.fallback: Coverage fallback uses only reliably decoded SMTP source agents for mandatory SMTP presence; independent malformed XMP does not invent a source mailbox.
nonsmtp_availability_review.boundary: No directory lookup, invented SMTP mailbox, complete source grammar or complete mixed-address normalization is inferred.

source_scope_coverage_review.basis: EA-PDF source coverage permits independent retained originals and unrendered emails. Source-derived Core Field presence and date conditions follow the selected email original, including a second catalog Source, rather than the first/global original. Unknown ownership stays unavailable; supplied schema and universal contradictions remain independent.
source_scope_coverage_review.boundary: Ordinary raw-address omission is optional and does not become required from an unrelated header. This review does not establish complete source/attachment occurrence ownership, candidate enumeration or source grammar.

nested_source_inventory_review.basis: EA-PDF 7.2 permits original assets containing additional unrendered emails. Known uninspected mail attachments and mailbox envelopes prevent a universal proof based only on outer headers. A scored outer match with a contradicted field remains tentative when these candidates exist.
nested_source_inventory_review.independent_checks: Consistent outer originals remain checkable; ordinary binary attachments do not imply nested email. Supplied schema failures retain their independent predicates.
nested_source_inventory_review.boundary: This guard does not enumerate nested sources, assign nested ownership, parse MSG/PST or certify arbitrary archive contents. Unavailable candidate comparisons remain INCOMPLETE.

downstream_source_binding_review.basis: The metadata pass establishes the pipeline source binding for each email record. Source-fidelity recommendations, ordered header inventories and source-derived native attachment aliases reuse that result, including unassigned ownership. They cannot independently rescore a rejected tentative original.
downstream_source_binding_review.boundary: An unavailable source cannot establish equality, alteration or a source-derived alias checksum. Supplied type errors, known-source recommendation differences and independent native observations retain their predicates. Standalone checks without a pipeline binding retain their documented source-scoring boundary.

external_sources_reviewed.conclusion: dc:creator is an ordered array of creator names; creators may be people, organizations or services. No software-only value constraint follows.
pdf:Producer identifies the tool creating the PDF; the schema does not prescribe product-name spelling.
xmp:CreateDate records resource creation; filesystem timestamps need not agree.

The declaration namespace is http://pdfa.org/declarations/. Document claims are scoped to that PDF, not its children. declarations is an unordered array of structured declarations; conformsTo is required, claimData optional. Actual conformance requires separate evidence.
The conformsTo URI separates its path and fragment with #. The registry identifier is distinct from a hyperlink anchor used in EA-PDF explanatory text.
The ISO/TS 32005 registry identifier is https://pdfa.org/declarations#iso32005. claimBy and claimDate are recommended, other claim fields optional; they are not additional mandatory EA-PDF fields.

issues.disposition: Treat RFC 8118 as a dated media-type reference. Do not infer PDF/A-4 or newer extension support from its older feature inventory, and do not invent a replacement RFC from an unresolved report.

issues.title: Typo in Standard Structure Elements Cheat Sheet for PDF 2.0 SSEs "Thead" - should be "THead"
issues.disposition: Use the standard THead spelling. A corrected cheat-sheet master is not evidence that a downloaded release changed. Generic structure validation remains upstream.

issues.title: "PDF/A in a Nutshell 2.0" is out of date
issues.disposition: The older PDF/A booklet is not the profile/edition authority. Continue using pinned actual veraPDF profiles and retain the PDF/A-4 edition question.

issues.title: PDF/A cheat sheets
issues.disposition: Cheat sheets are supporting explanations, not a replacement for normative clauses or actual profile predicates; no runtime change follows the editorial comments.

issues.title: Typo in errata in sponsored ISO 32000-2:2020 Errata Collection 2
issues.disposition: Track the EC2 annotation typo RP versus EP as a source-publication defect. Comments confirm correction in EC3; do not claim the pinned EC2 copy was replaced or that EC3 was downloaded.

issues.title: EA-PDF v1.0 spec PDF is technically invalid (number tree has odd number of entries)
issues.disposition: The pinned EA-PDF publication contains two odd-length number-tree arrays, including the reported object. Preserve its content hash, use its text as specification evidence, and exclude its bytes as a positive conformance fixture.

issues.title: Sponsored EC2 PDF is technically invalid (attached files have Subtype in EF)
issues.disposition: Subtype belongs on the embedded-file stream, not the EF dictionary. Record the EC2 publication defect and EC3 resolution comment; do not copy the malformed publication object or add a duplicate generic PDF/A validator.

issues.title: Typo in EA-PDF v1.0
issues.disposition: Treat PDF/A-4fe in the overview as a reported editorial typo. The normative allowed-flavour table and current engine accept 4e, never a new 4fe flavour.

issues.title: WTPDF 1.0 outline hierachy in the PDF is incorrectly indented - H3 is merged with H2
issues.disposition: The WTPDF publication outline indentation defect does not change EA-PDF obligations.

issues.title: PDF Declarations does not provide advice or schema for PDF/A-4
issues.disposition: The missing PDF/A-4 declaration-schema example is a dependency limitation, not permission to require a nonexistent RELAX NG artifact or reuse the PDF/A-3 extension schema unconditionally. Keep EA-PDF declaration semantics and upstream syntax separate.

issues.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - requirements for DPM metadata in table 8 are invalid
issues.disposition: The reported DPM-name prohibition is superseded by published ISO-approved erratum 86, which permits name values and requires their decoded bytes to be UTF-8. Retain Table 8 names; do not implement the proposed text-string replacement. DPM traversal/name decoding coverage remains a dependency follow-up.

issues.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - minor issues
issues.disposition: Retain the published NonFullScreenPageMode SHALL despite the removal proposal. Flag ambiguous Source-AF cardinality for expert review. Keep asset ContentType/Checksum distinct from attachment Content-Type/CheckSum; the naming complaint is not authorization to rename fields. Corrected paraphrases need not reproduce the editorial spelling typo.

issues.title: Typo in text of errata annotation of ISO 32000-2 sponsored editon 2
issues.disposition: The EC2 annotation wording was corrected after review to retain the word text. Use the final normative erratum, not an intermediate comment or base-text extraction that omits annotations.

issues.title: Spurious “24T” characters in the Type 2 function formula in Table 40 of ISO 32000-2 PDF when zoomed
issues.disposition: The tiny formula artifact is a publication/rendering defect, not a new EA-PDF requirement or a reason to copy the malformed formula. Generic PDF graphics constraints remain upstream.

issues.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - minor issue (with collections)
issues.disposition: Keep Bcc in the required collection schema, allowing an explicitly blank message value; the member comment explains that preservation intent. Track Size/source-byte semantics and the Table 5/6 Message-ID discrepancy for expert review. Retain Table 6 requirements pending disposition.

issues.title: Consider adding a Form/Action/Digitial Signature page and a Multimedia/Richmedia/3D page to PDF cheatsheets
issues.disposition: A request for new forms/signatures/multimedia cheat sheets does not add EA-PDF file-format requirements.

issues.title: iso 32000-2 Errata clause 12 webpage is a bit incorrect.
issues.disposition: The generic form CharSet version-label editorial fix has no EA-PDF-specific runtime delta. Use current normative references when forms are reviewed.

issues.title: Another mention of a table has changed caption.
issues.disposition: The encryption-table caption correction is reference maintenance, not permission to change encryption policy. Generic encryption restrictions stay upstream.

issues.title: EA-PDF - requirements when the PDF/A-4 file is tagged.
issues.disposition: Record RoleMap/RoleMapNS scope and placement concerns against the existing question. Do not downgrade ISO/TS 32005 SHALL to SHOULD, remove required maps, or require optional PDF/UA-2 because an open issue proposes a different policy. The issue body reverses the first Table 9 pair compared with the pinned PDF; preserve the pinned Artifact-to-Private mapping.

issues.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - more minor issues
issues.disposition: Keep exactly integer ExtensionLevel 5 with BaseVersion name 1.7; do not adopt the proposed >=5 rule. Date comments are not a published amendment: preserve EA-PDF 9.8 creation-date wording, but remove inferred PASS/FAIL based solely on comparison with source Sent and report unavailable independent provenance.

issues.title: Accessibility issues with the Hierarchical inclusion rules excel document
issues.disposition: Record accessibility concerns in the supplementary ISO/TS 32005 spreadsheet as source QA. They do not invalidate the standard inclusion rules, establish that a profile ran, or mandate PDF/UA in EA-PDF.

issues.title: Improvement suggestion for pdfa.org site
issues.disposition: Use canonical section anchors for declarations and extensions. Heading-link UI suggestions do not change the referenced declaration definitions.

issues.title: Accessibility of Alt and Contents for Link Annotations, with Brotli document
issues.disposition: The discussion concerns links in the Brotli publication and PDF/UA/WTPDF goals. It does not make PDF/UA conformance or Alt on every EA-PDF annotation mandatory; retain the separate EA-PDF attachment Contents question.

issues.title: Add QuadPoints definition to the glossary
issues.disposition: A draft glossary explanation is not a conformance amendment. Rect and QuadPoints semantics are subtype-specific; do not add QuadPoints to FileAttachment or require it on every link based on this discussion.
